text.p: The Turkish central bank injected a total of 23.7 trillion lira into a cash-strapped market via overnight money and eight-day repos on Wednesday.

It lent banks 16.3 trillion lira overnight at 75 percent after injecting 7.37 trillion lira via eight-day repos at an average rate of 74.29 percent in the morning as the market opened 15 trillion lira short.

Bankers said cash demand was strong because of the banks' weekly liquidity requirements and money demand after the holiday. The markets had closed for Republic day after one hour of trade on Monday morning.
"Cash demand may continue to rise tomorrow because further cash outflow is expected due to value added tax payments," a private banker said.

The Turkish lira closed slightly firmer at 95,900 to the dollar after fluctuating during the day amid volatility in international markets. It opened up at 95,750 after Monday's 95,930 close due to a lower dollar/mark parity, but later eased.
T-bill yields firmed on cash shortage and also in correction of sharp falls prompted on Friday by record bid and sale and sharply lower yields at the Treasury's one-year bond auction.

The Treasury had sold 311.1 trillion lira worth of October 30, 1997 papers at an average yield of 121.77 percent with today's value. The average yield on the one-year bonds had plunged by about four points on Friday afternoon.
Banks paid 136.7 trillion lira to the treasury today for the one-year bonds in return for 140 trillion lira of maturing t-bills.

The average yield on the most heavily traded October 30, 1997 bond firmed to 117.50 percent from Monday's 117.27. In papers having shorter maturities, yields rose by around one point on liquidity shortage.
